newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ING Barings says Brazil trade gap worrisome.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings says Brazil trade gap worrisome.

text.p: ING Barings said Monday Brazil's trade deficit was becoming worrisome and that it expected the government to adopt restrictive measures by the middle of the year.
ING Barings said in a report the trade gap was expected to reach over $4.0 billion in the three months just ended compared with a balanced account a year ago.

"ING Barings' Brazil Economists Jose Carlos de Faria and Guilherme Abbud write that the latest figures and estimates suggest that the country could soon be running an external imbalance of worrisome proportions," the statement said.
It said it foresaw a current account deficit in 1997 of $30 billion. In 1996, Brazil's current account gap was $24.3 billion, equivalent to 3.27 percent of gross domestic product.
"It is not clear whether this is because the economy accelerated unduly or because structural changes have pushed the propensity to import way up," ING Barings said.
ING Barings said the government had several economic tools it could use and next year's presidential and congressional elections would be a factor in determining the timing of any action.
"If the external deficit does not soon improve, it is ING Barings' view that the government will impose monetary, credit and possibly even import restrictions by mid-year," the report said.
